1|# Design: task 5 contracts and scene reader
2|
3|Goal: define module contracts so music generation never blocks the reader, then build the scene reader with two placeholder tracks. Real tracks drop in later by replacing files only. Branch `contracts-reader`. Binding inputs: AGENTS.md, SECURITY.md, `core/types.ts`, `core/cluster.ts`, `next.config.ts`, `data/books/oz/music-clusters.json`. This step writes only this doc. The implementer writes `docs/contracts.md`, `core/music.ts`, the manifest, the reader, and the tests.
4|
5|## Module layout
6|
7|```text
8|core/
9|  types.ts    existing book, scene, emotion shapes plus new contract types
10|  music.ts    MusicManifest, Track, parseManifest, selectTrack, nextAlternative
11|  reader.ts   ReaderModel, buildReaderModel
12|  cluster.ts  unchanged, lends buildFeatures to music.ts
13|server/
14|  books.ts    server-only loader: reads oz json, returns Book plus scenes
15|app/
16|  page.tsx    server component: loads data, builds model, renders text
17|  reader.tsx  client container: observer, selection, override, manifest fetch
18|  player/     client player: audio elements, controls, crossfade
19|  tokens.css  unchanged unless a player style needs a token
20|public/music/
21|  manifest.json   placeholder manifest, version 1
22|  README.md       swap guide plus CC-BY-NC note
23|  placeholder/    two mp3 clips, already present
24|```
25|
26|Ownership: `core` is pure and owns every shared type plus selection and model building. `server` owns file reads and env. `app` owns rendering and playback. Import direction is `core <- server` and `core <- app`. Neither `server` nor client components import each other. `app/page.tsx` may import `server/books.ts`. Client files never do.
27|
28|## Core types and signatures
29|
30|New file `core/music.ts`. It reuses `Vector8`, `EMOTIONS`, `FEATURE_WEIGHTS`, and `buildFeatures` from `core/types.ts` and `core/cluster.ts`. Choice: reuse `buildFeatures` in place because `cluster.ts` imports only types, so client code gains no Node or heavy code.
31|
32|```ts
33|export interface Track {
34|  id: string; src: string; label: string;
35|  vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number;
36|  durationSec: number; loop: boolean;
37|}
38|export interface MusicManifest { version: number; tracks: Track[]; }
39|export function parseManifest(json: unknown): MusicManifest;
40|export function selectTrack(
41|  scene: { vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number } | null,
42|  manifest: MusicManifest,
43|  currentTrackId?: string | null,
44|  opts?: { margin?: number; exclude?: string[] },
45|): Track | null;
46|export function nextAlternative(
47|  scene: { vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number } | null,
48|  manifest: MusicManifest,
49|  currentTrackId: string | null,
50|): Track | null;
51|```
52|
53|Rules from the spec: `parseManifest` throws on unknown version, missing fields, a vector not over the 8 ids, numbers outside 0..1, or a `src` that is not a `/music/` relative path or https URL. `selectTrack` scores cosine similarity over `buildFeatures` output, keeps the current track unless the best beats it by `margin` (default 0.05), returns null for a null scene with no current track, returns null for an empty manifest, and breaks ties by manifest order. `nextAlternative` ranks by similarity after the current track and wraps around, so repeats cycle all tracks; one track returns itself. When `scene` is null it ranks on the current track first, which keeps playback stable through failed scenes.
54|
55|Contract-only types live in `core/types.ts`, with no routes and no implementations:
56|
57|```ts
58|export interface ImageRequest { bookId: string; textVersion: string; firstN: number; lastN: number; }
59|export interface ImageResponse { url: string; }
60|export interface ChatRequest { bookId: string; textVersion: string; positionN: number; spoilerMode: boolean; messages: { role: "user" | "assistant"; text: string }[]; }
61|```
62|
63|Quota and budget stay server-only: integer micro-dollars, Redis `INCRBY` reserve before each model call, `DECRBY` refund after. Clients never see keys or raw errors. Image cache key is `firstN..lastN` plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion` at a deterministic Blob path checked with `head()`; routes return URLs, never bytes.
64|
65|## Reader model shape
66|
67|New pure function in `core/reader.ts`:
68|
69|```ts
70|export interface ReaderParagraph { id: string; n: number; text: string; }
71|export interface ReaderScene {
72|  id: string; title: string;
73|  emotion: { vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number } | null;
74|  paragraphs: ReaderParagraph[];
75|}
76|export interface ReaderChapter { ch: number; title: string; scenes: ReaderScene[]; }
77|export interface ReaderModel {
78|  bookId: string; textVersion: string; title: string; author: string;
79|  chapters: ReaderChapter[];
80|}
81|export function buildReaderModel(
82|  book: Pick<Book, "id" | "title" | "author" | "chapters" | "paragraphs" | "textVersion">,
83|  analysis: { scenes: AnalyzedScene[] },
84|): ReaderModel;
85|```
86|
87|It joins paragraphs to scenes by `n` ranges in reading order, keeps `final` emotion or null for failed scenes, and drops analysis internals (`jev`, `muse_override`, provenance) so they never reach the client. It throws on unordered scenes or on paragraphs covered zero or two times, reusing the checks in `core/scenes.ts` where they fit.
88|
89|## Server side
90|
91|`server/books.ts` starts with `import 'server-only'` and exposes one function:
92|
93|```ts
94|export function loadOzBook(): { book: Book; scenes: AnalyzedScene[] };
95|```
96|
97|It reads `data/books/oz/book.json`, `scenes.json`, and `analysis.json` with a static import (build time, no request cost) and returns typed values. `app/page.tsx` calls it, runs `buildReaderModel`, and renders chapters, scene sections, and paragraphs as server HTML. Paragraph ids reuse `paragraphId` from `core/ids.ts`, which yields `c12p34` style ids. Choice: text renders on the server and only scene ids plus emotion triples pass as props to client components, so the full book text never duplicates in the client payload.
98|
99|## App side
100|
101|`app/page.tsx` owns layout: centered book column at the reading measure, quiet side panel with the "Chat comes later." placeholder, and the player bar slot. No chat code. Scene sections carry `data-scene-id` with a subtle divider and no other chrome.
102|
103|`app/reader.tsx` is the client container. It owns the manifest fetch (once, from `/music/manifest.json`, parsed with `parseManifest`), the active scene id, the current track id, and the skip override. On manifest failure the reader still renders and the bar shows a short neutral message. It passes the chosen track to the player.
104|
105|`app/player/` owns only playback: audio elements, play state, volume, and the skip button wired through an `onSkip` prop from the container.
106|
107|## Active scene tracking
108|
109|One `IntersectionObserver` watches scene sections. The reading line sits near the top third of the viewport, set with a `rootMargin` band around minus 30 percent. The active scene is the intersecting section whose top edge is nearest above the line. Choice: observer with a band instead of scroll math because jumps and fast scrolls then resolve in one callback with no position cache to maintain. Edge handling: short scenes still cross the band since sections span their paragraphs; when nothing intersects (fast fling between frames), keep the last active scene rather than guessing. On mount, compute from current scroll position so reloads mid book start on the right scene.
110|
111|## Player state machine
112|
113|States: `idle`, `playing`, `paused`, `crossfading`, `no music`. `idle` means no user gesture yet; `no music` means the manifest failed or is empty.
114|
115|```text
116|idle --press play--> playing (or crossfading when a track is already selected)
117|playing --track change--> crossfading --1.5s--> playing
118|playing --press pause--> paused --press play--> playing
119|any --manifest failure or empty--> no music
120|```
121|
122|Two `audio` elements fade against each other on change over about 1.5 s, then the old one pauses. `prefers-reduced-motion` sets the fade to 0. Choice: plain audio elements with a volume ramp instead of Web Audio because nothing here needs decoding or filtering, and native elements keep codec and loop behavior free. Loop is on. Audio starts only after the user presses play, which satisfies autoplay rules; track swaps before first press only change `src`. Volume slider sets both elements. UI motion stays under 200 ms per tokens; the audio fade is not UI motion. Controls are real buttons with labels, visible focus, and full keyboard use. The bar shows the track label and the active scene title.
123|
124|## Selection and skip override
125|
126|On each active scene change the container runs `selectTrack(sceneEmotion, manifest, currentId)` and stores the result as current. The "Change track" button calls `nextAlternative` and stores that id as the override for the current scene. While the override stands, scene rerenders reuse it without calling `selectTrack`. When the active scene changes, the override clears and selection runs again with the override track passed as `currentTrackId`, so hysteresis compares against what the user last heard. This matches the product rule that a skip holds until the next scene.
127|
128|## Placeholder manifest
129|
130|Choice: static `public/music/manifest.json` fetched by the client, because it needs no route, ships from the CDN, and a later swap replaces files only. `version: 1`, two tracks, `loop: true`, `durationSec: 10`:
131|
132|| Track | File | Label | Emotion source |
133||-------|------|-------|----------------|
134|| oz-test-01 | placeholder/oz-test-01-calma-t01.mp3 | Calm, flute and harp | cluster t01, intensity 0.229, tempo 0.245 |
135|| oz-test-02 | placeholder/oz-test-02-suspenso-t07.mp3 | Suspense, tremolo strings | cluster t07, intensity 0.530, tempo 0.539 |
136|
137|Vectors copy the t01 and t07 centroids rounded to 3 decimals; both already sum to 1.000 at that rounding, and the implementer renormalizes if any edit shifts the sum. `public/music/README.md` covers the swap (replace files and manifest, keep the shape, bump version) plus the CC-BY-NC note for MusicGen output in this non-commercial demo. One test loads the committed manifest through `parseManifest` and asserts every `src` exists under `public/`.
138|
139|## Test list
140|
141|Vitest, beside the code, no DOM library. `core/music.test.ts`: nearest by cosine wins; hysteresis keeps current within margin and switches beyond it; null scene keeps current and returns null without one; empty manifest returns null; `exclude` skips ids; ties follow manifest order; `nextAlternative` cycles all tracks and returns the single track to itself; `parseManifest` accepts the good manifest and rejects each bad shape. `core/reader.test.ts`: reading order, scenes ordered by `n`, every paragraph exactly once, null emotion for failed scenes, no `jev` or `muse_override` fields in output. Manifest test as above. Player and observer logic that can be pure stays pure and tested; the rest is covered by `next build` plus a manual run.
142|
143|## Risks
144|
145|Autoplay: browsers block sound before gesture, so the player must never call play on mount or on track change while `idle`; verify by loading and confirming silence until press. Observer: `find in page` and anchor jumps can set odd scroll positions, so the mount computation plus the keep-last fallback matter more than band tuning. Page weight: the full Oz text ships as server HTML, which is the point of a reader, but keep images and the manifest out of the critical path so first paint stays text. CSP: current `media-src 'self' blob:` and `connect-src 'self'` already cover `/music/` files and the manifest fetch, so no CSP change; note that future remote https track URLs would need a `media-src` edit, and the validator allows them only for that future.
146|
147|## Fix pass
148|
149|Review findings 1 to 9 are fixed, 10 is now a motion state with a change
150|listener (visuals only, never the audio fade), and 11 went away with the
151|player rewrite. Manifest is version 2 with hand-labeled `emotion` per
152|track, `title` instead of `label`, and optional `startSec`, `loop`,
153|`source`, and attribution fields. `SceneEmotion` is now `SceneSignal`.
154|Similarity is pluggable (`bhattacharyyaSimilarity` by default,
155|`cosineSimilarity` kept), tuned through `MUSIC_CONFIG`. A pure scheduler
156|in `core/music-schedule.ts` owns dwell, hysteresis, hard cuts, and the
157|same-emotion Next rule; the reader calls it with wall-clock seconds.
158|The player uses two audio elements with equal-power `requestAnimationFrame`
159|fades, ref-held volume, `startSec` seeks, and internal re-looping for
160|long tracks. Docs follow `docs/contracts.md`.
161|
162|## Decisions where the spec was open
163|
164|- Reuse `buildFeatures` from `core/cluster.ts` without moving it: the module imports only types, so it adds nothing unsuitable to the client bundle.
165|- Static manifest over a route: fewer moving parts and the swap stays files only.
166|- Observer band over scroll math: correct on jumps with no cache to maintain.
167|- Two audio elements with volume ramp over Web Audio: no decode code for zero audible gain.
168|- Hysteresis default 0.05: stops flicker between neighboring scenes while real mood shifts still switch.
169|- Server-rendered text with slim client props: full text reaches the reader once, without doubling in the client payload.

1|# Review: task 5 contracts and scene reader
2|
3|Verdict: fix finding 1 first. The reader renders and plays, but slow scrolling never moves the music to the next scene. Findings 2 to 6 should land in the same pass; 7 to 11 are nits.
4|
5|What this change does: adds the module contracts in `docs/contracts.md`, pure track selection and manifest parsing in `core/music.ts`, the slim reader model in `core/reader.ts`, a server-only Oz loader in `server/books.ts`, and the client reader (`app/reader.tsx`, `app/active-scene.ts`, `app/player.tsx`) with a two-track placeholder manifest in `public/music/`.
6|
7|## Findings
8|
9|1. **Slow scroll down never advances the active scene** (blocker), `app/reader.tsx:107-119`, `app/active-scene.ts:10-25`.
10|   Problem: the observer callback scores only the changed entries. A new scene enters the 5 percent band from below with its top under the reading line, so `pickActiveScene` skips it. Its top then crosses the line with no further callback (intersection status does not change), and when the old scene exits, the old entry is filtered out and the result falls back to current. The next scene is adopted only when its top is already above the line at entry, which is the scroll-up direction plus jumps, not scroll-down.
11|   Fix: use entries only as a trigger and re-snapshot all sections with live rects on each callback, as the mount path already does. Derive the hit flag from rect versus band in the snapshot mapper.
12|
13|2. **Pause during a crossfade leaves the incoming element playing** (should-fix), `app/player.tsx:61-80`.
14|   Problem: `toggle` pauses only the live element. For 1.5 s after a track change the standby element is the audible one, so pressing pause in that window sets state to paused while audio keeps playing.
15|   Fix: pause both refs in `toggle`, or keep the fading pair in one ref both handlers use.
16|
17|3. **Volume sits in the track-effect deps and restarts fades** (should-fix), `app/player.tsx:28-59`.
18|   Problem: every slider tick re-runs the track effect. While paused the early return does not apply (live is paused), so each tick reassigns `standby.src` and flips `liveRef`. Mid-fade it also reassigns the incoming `src`, which reloads that track from zero, and starts a fresh interval.
19|   Fix: drop `volume` from the deps, read it through a ref inside the fade, and return early when the live element already carries the track `src` regardless of paused state.
20|
21|4. **Validator accepts NaN vector entries** (should-fix), `core/music.ts:34-37`.
22|   Problem: `isVector8` checks `typeof` only, and `typeof NaN` is `number`. A NaN entry passes `parseManifest`, then poisons the cosine score and the sort order for that track.
23|   Fix: require `Number.isFinite` for each of the 8 values, one word in the same check.
24|
25|5. **Tests skip the behaviors the brief asked about** (should-fix), `core/music.test.ts`, `app/reader.tsx:36-61`.
26|   Problem: no test covers `nextAlternative` with a null scene, `selectTrack` with an excluded current track, the skip override held until the scene change and then used as current, or reselection when the manifest lands after the first scene. The observer wiring has no test beyond the pure picker.
27|   Fix: add the three core cases (null scene alternative, excluded current, excluded all) and pull `applyScene` into a pure helper beside `active-scene.ts` with two tests: override as base on scene change, cleared after.
28|
29|6. **Doc says the reader consumes `scenes.json`, code never reads it** (should-fix), `docs/contracts.md:11-20`, `server/books.ts:9-17`.
30|   Problem: `loadOzBook` reads `book.json` plus `analysis.json` only, which is fine because analysis carries every scene field, but the contract lists `scenes.json` as an input the reader consumes.
31|   Fix: name `analysis.json` as the scene source and `scenes.json` as the pipeline intermediate it mirrors, in one sentence.
32|
33|7. **Tie-break repeats an index scan per comparison** (nit), `core/music.ts:96-99`.
34|   Problem: the comparator calls `manifest.tracks.indexOf` on each tie. Sort is already stable, so ties follow manifest order without it.
35|   Fix: delete the tie branch and return the diff.
36|
37|8. **Two `SceneEmotion` types with different shapes** (nit), `core/music.ts:22-26`, `core/types.ts:78-83`.
38|   Problem: `core/music.ts` exports `SceneEmotion` as `{ vector, intensity, tempo }` while `core/types.ts` uses the same name for `{ jev, muse_override, final, error }`. Each reads fine alone; importing both invites the wrong one.
39|   Fix: rename the music one to `SceneSignal` or reuse an inline param type.
40|
41|9. **Snapshot helper takes a flag it never varies** (nit), `app/reader.tsx:31, 101-106`.
42|   Problem: `snapshot(hit)` is called once with `true`, and `byId.current` is rebuilt on every render.
43|   Fix: delete the parameter and build the map with `useMemo` on `scenes`.
44|
45|10. **Reduced-motion choice never updates** (nit), `app/player.tsx:26`.
46|    Problem: `matchMedia` runs per render with no listener, so flipping the OS setting mid session keeps the old fade until a rerender for another reason.
47|    Fix: read it once in state with a change listener, or leave it; the wrongness lasts one session at most.
48|
49|11. **Track swap mid-fade restarts from partial volumes** (nit), `app/player.tsx:43-56`.
50|    Problem: the cleanup clears the old interval but leaves the old live element at partial volume, and the new run fades from there while the incoming `src` is replaced. Playback converges, only the fade curve kinks.
51|    Fix: nothing required once finding 3 lands; note it only if the effect is reworked anyway.
52|
53|## Checked and fine
54|
55|- Core purity: no `process.env`, `node:` imports, `fetch`, or `fs` in `core/` outside tests. Import direction holds: `app/page.tsx` imports `server/books.ts`, client files import only `core/` and siblings, `server/books.ts` starts with `import 'server-only'`.

58|- Manifest trust boundary: the client parses every fetch with `parseManifest`, which rejects unknown versions, missing fields, short vectors, out-of-range numbers, and non-`/music/` non-https `src`. Bad drop-ins fail loudly.
59|- CSP unchanged and sufficient: `media-src 'self' blob:` covers the placeholder clips, `connect-src 'self'` covers the manifest fetch. Both docs note remote https tracks need a `media-src` edit.
60|- Reading line consistent with the band: the band spans 30 to 35 percent of viewport height, the line sits at one third, inside the band. Short scenes still cross it because sections span their paragraphs.
61|- Swap guide: `public/music/README.md` replaces files plus manifest plus version bump, names `parseManifest` as the shape check, and carries the CC-BY-NC non-commercial note. Swap needs no code change.
62|- Design: styles use tokens only (all names exist in `app/tokens.css`), accent is Meta blue on borders and focus, no purple or gradients, controls are real buttons and inputs with labels and visible focus, no UI transition over 200 ms (audio fade is not UI motion).
63|- Prose: `docs/contracts.md` and the README are short, sentence case, no filler or banned words.
64|- Runs: `npm test` 63/63 across 14 files, `npm run typecheck` clean, `npm run build` clean with `/` prerendered static.
65|
66|## Not checked
67|
68|- Audible playback, real scroll behavior, and screen-reader pass were not run; the observer finding rests on reading plus band math, not a browser session. Live manifest fetch against the built server was not repeated.
69|
70|## Round 2
71|
72|What this change does: the fix pass answers findings 1 to 10, adds manifest v2 with hand-labeled emotions, a pure scheduler with dwell/hysteresis/min-track/hard-cut, same-emotion Next, and a two-element player rewrite with loop crossfades and attribution. The rules all land. Three player/scheduler defects do not.
73|

75|
76|1. **Reader skip choice reverts on the same scene** (breaks Martin's rule), `core/music-schedule.ts:60-100, 151-166`.
77|   Problem: `evaluateSwitch` never reads `overrideId`, and `tickScheduler` re-runs it every second. After Change track the override is a dead field: it is set in `requestNext` (`music-schedule.ts:185-186`) and cleared in `promote`, but nothing checks it.
78|   Case (run against the real scheduler): scene pure tristeza, tracks pure/bland tristeza plus calm; Next moves pure to bland with gap 0.145, then `tickScheduler` at 45 s after the press switches back to pure on the same scene, stale `overrideId: bland` still set. Gaps at or above `hardCutMargin` revert within one second instead. The committed fixture hides this only because its same-emotion gaps sit below `switchMargin`.
79|   Fix: in `tickScheduler`, when there is no pending scene and `overrideId` is set, return `noChange` without the re-check. Pending promotion still clears the override. Add the missing test: override versus a mid-gap scene holds past `minTrackSec`.
80|   If we skip it: the Change track button undoes itself, worst on scenes where the reader's pick scores far below best.
81|
82|2. **Loop fade restarts on every timeupdate for 3 s** (audible stutter, repeated reloads), `app/player.tsx:86, 145-157`.
83|   Problem: `handleTimeUpdate` arms `loopArmedRef` then calls `requestPlayRef`, whose first lines clear `loopArmedRef` back to null. 84|   Case: any looping track within `crossfadeSec` of its end fires timeupdate about 4 times per second; each one restarts the 3 s loop fade.
85|   Fix: delete the unconditional clear at line 86 and clear the arm only on a real track change, e.g. guard it with `trackRef.current?.id !== next.id` before the assignment. One line.
86|   If we skip it: every loop point stutters instead of crossfading.

89|   Problem: first-press `toggle` calls `requestPlay(next, 0)`, then the `[started, trackId]` effect fires on the same track and calls `requestPlay(next, fadeSec)`. When the scheduler already switched pre-press, `fadeSec` can be 3, so the track crossfades into itself on the other element. Even at 0 the `src` is assigned twice.
90|   Fix: remove the direct `requestPlay` call from the first-press branch and let the effect do the single start. Note in the diff that a pre-press scheduler switch then gives a 3 s fade-in on first press; force 0 there if Martin wants instant start.
91|   If we skip it: readers who read a while before pressing play hear the track restart into itself.
92|
93|### Should fix

32|```ts
33|export interface Track {
34|  id: string; src: string; label: string;
35|  vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number;
36|  durationSec: number; loop: boolean;
37|}
38|export interface MusicManifest { version: number; tracks: Track[]; }
39|export function parseManifest(json: unknown): MusicManifest;
40|export function selectTrack(

100|

102|
103|`app/reader.tsx` is the client container. 104|
105|`app/player/` owns only playback: audio elements, play state, volume, and the skip button wired through an `onSkip` prop from the container.
106|
107|## Active scene tracking
108|
109|One `IntersectionObserver` watches scene sections. The reading line sits near the top third of the viewport, set with a `rootMargin` band around minus 30 percent. 110|

112|
113|States: `idle`, `playing`, `paused`, `crossfading`, `no music`. `idle` means no user gesture yet; `no music` means the manifest failed or is empty.

144|
145|Autoplay: browsers block sound before gesture, so the player must never call play on mount or on track change while `idle`; verify by loading and confirming silence until press. 1|# Contracts
2|
3|Music generation must never block the reader. Each module below owns one
4|job and can be swapped without touching the others. Import direction is
5|`core <- server` and `core <- app`. Server and client components never
6|import each other. `app/page.tsx` may import `server/books.ts`. Client
7|files never do.
8|
9|## Book data
10|
11|`data/books/oz/book.json` holds the frozen text: id, title, author,
12|`textVersion` hash, chapters with `start_n` and `end_n`, and paragraphs
13|with `id`, `ch`, `n`, and `text`. `analysis.json` is the scene source
14|the reader consumes: the same scenes plus Jev vectors, the Muse
15|override, and the `final` emotion. `scenes.json` is the pipeline
16|intermediate that `analysis.json` mirrors. The reader consumes the book
17|fields, scene ranges and titles, and the `final` vector with intensity
18|and tempo. It never sees `jev`, `muse_override`, or provenance.
19|`core/reader.ts` defines `buildReaderModel`, which joins paragraphs to
20|scenes by ordinal range and throws on unordered scenes or on paragraphs
21|covered zero or two times.
22|
23|## Music library
24|
25|The library is a static `public/music/manifest.json`, version 2, fetched
26|by the client from `/music/manifest.json`. A static file needs no route,
27|ships from the CDN, and swaps by replacing files only. Tracks may be
28|several minutes long and are not loops unless marked so.
29|
30|`MusicManifest = { version, tracks }`. `Track = { id, src, title,
31|emotion, vector, intensity, tempo, durationSec }` plus optional
32|`startSec` (default 0, where playback starts on first play and on each
33|loop), `loop` (default true), `source` (`generated`, `jamendo`, or
34|`recording`), `artist`, `composer`, `license`, `attribution`, and
35|`sourceUrl` (https only). `emotion` is the hand label: one of the 8
36|emotion ids in `core/types.ts`. The vector covers the 8 ids with finite
37|entries in 0..1. `core/music.ts` owns `parseManifest`, which rejects
38|unknown versions, missing fields, bad vectors, NaN entries, out-of-range
39|numbers, `startSec` outside its range, unknown `source` values, and any
40|`src` that is not a `/music/` path or `https` URL. The reader calls it on
41|every fetch, so a bad drop-in fails loudly in dev. Remote URLs need a
42|`media-src` addition in `next.config.ts`.
43|
44|## Similarity and config
45|
46|`Similarity = (scene: SceneSignal, track: Track) => number`, where
47|`SceneSignal = { vector, intensity, tempo }`. The default is
48|`bhattacharyyaSimilarity`: both 8-emotion vectors renormalize to sum 1
49|(an all-zero vector gives an affinity of 0), `E` is the sum of
50|`sqrt(s_k * t_k)`, and the score is `0.70 * E` plus `0.15` each for
51|intensity and tempo closeness. `cosineSimilarity` over `buildFeatures`
52|output stays as an exported alternative. One exported object,
53|`MUSIC_CONFIG`, holds `similarity`, `weights`, `switchMargin` (0.07),
54|`dwellSec` (20), `minTrackSec` (45), `hardCutMargin` (0.20),
55|`crossfadeSec` (3), and `hardCutCrossfadeSec` (1.5). Everything else
56|reads from it. Ranking ties go to the lower track id.
57|
58|## Selection scheduler
59|
60|`core/music-schedule.ts` is a pure state machine. The reader calls
61|`observeScene`, `tickScheduler`, `requestNext`, and `noteTrackEnded`
62|with explicit `nowSec` values, so all timing is testable without
63|timers. State holds the current track id and when it started, the active
64|scene id, the pending scene id and since when, and the skip override
65|with the scene it belongs to.
66|
67|A newly entered scene becomes pending and the dwell clock restarts, so
68|fast scrolling keeps only the newest scene. The first track ever plays
69|at once with no dwell. After the pending scene holds for `dwellSec` it
70|becomes active and the override clears. Then the best track switches in
71|only when it beats the current score by `switchMargin` and the current
72|track played `minTrackSec`, unless it wins by `hardCutMargin` (hard
73|cut, short fade). A second passes the active scene back through the
74|switch check, so a hold from `minTrackSec` releases on time. A switch
75|reports its crossfade length: 3 s normally,
76|1.5 s for hard cuts. The skip choice holds until the next scene change;
77|after that, dwell and hysteresis apply with the override track as the
78|current track. A null scene means a failed analysis with no vector, so
79|it never triggers a switch. A non-looping track that ends fades into
80|the best remaining track, excluding the one that ended.
81|
82|## Change track
83|
84|`nextTrack` cycles tracks hand-labeled with the scene dominant emotion
85|(argmax of the renormalized scene vector, ties by emotion order), ranked
86|by score with ties by lower id, wrapping around and skipping the current
87|track. When the current track has another emotion, it starts at the top
88|candidate. With no other same-emotion track it falls back to the best
89|track overall that is not current. A null scene cycles all tracks in id
90|order. One track or none gives null, and the UI disables the button.
91|
92|## Player
93|
94|`app/player.tsx` takes the track, the fade length for the latest switch,
95|the scene title, a skip flag, and callbacks. It owns two `audio`
96|elements, play state, volume, and the equal-power crossfade
97|(cos/sin gains over the fade time, driven by `requestAnimationFrame`).
98|It never uses the `loop` attribute. Volume lives in a ref, so the slider
99|never re-runs the track effect or touches `src`. A new track request
100|mid-fade cancels the pending fade and fades from the audible element to
101|the newest track. On load each track seeks to `startSec` once metadata
102|is available. Long tracks with `loop` true crossfade into the other
103|element playing the same track from `startSec` when `currentTime`
104|reaches `duration - crossfadeSec`. When `loop` is false the player
105|reports the end and the scheduler picks the next-best track excluding
106|the ended one. Pause stops both elements; play resumes the audible one.
107|Audio starts only after the user presses play. Reduced motion is read in
108|state with a change listener and affects visuals only, never the fade.
109|
110|The bar shows Play/Pause, Volume, a Change track button (disabled when
111|Next has nothing to offer), the track title with its emotion label, and
112|attribution when present: composer or artist, license, and a source
113|link. On manifest failure the reader still renders and the bar shows a
114|short neutral note. UI motion stays under 200 ms. Controls are real
115|buttons and inputs with labels, visible focus, and keyboard use.
116|
117|## Image api
118|
119|Contract only, no routes. Request `{ bookId, textVersion, firstN, lastN
120|}` names the selection by touched paragraph ordinals. Response `{ url }`
121|is a Vercel Blob URL. The cache key is `firstN..lastN` plus
122|`textVersion` plus `promptVersion` at a deterministic Blob path with
123|`addRandomSuffix: false`. The server checks the path with `head()`
124|before generating and never returns bytes. The same paragraph range
125|reuses the image. Types live in `core/types.ts`.
126|
127|## Chat api
128|
129|Contract only, no routes. Request `{ bookId, textVersion, positionN,
130|spoilerMode, messages }` carries the chat history and the reader
131|position. The response is streamed text. The server builds context from
132|the book text up to `positionN`, or the whole book when `spoilerMode` is
133|on, with the book prefix first and the question last so readers share
134|the prompt cache. The system prompt answers only from that text and
135|refuses the rest. Types live in `core/types.ts`.
136|
137|## Quotas and budget
138|
139|Server only. Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars: reserve with
140|Redis `INCRBY` before each model call, refund with `DECRBY` after, one
141|reserve per call including retries. The server clamps every model tool
142|argument. Clients never see keys or raw errors. Generic messages go to
143|the client, details stay in server logs.

38|unknown versions, missing fields, bad vectors, NaN entries, out-of-range
39|numbers, `startSec` outside its range, unknown `source` values, and any
40|`src` that is not a `/music/` path or `https` URL. The reader calls it on
41|every fetch, so a bad drop-in fails loudly in dev. Remote URLs need a
42|`media-src` addition in `next.config.ts`.
43|
44|## Similarity and config
45|
46|`Similarity = (scene: SceneSignal, track: Track) => number`, where
47|`SceneSignal = { vector, intensity, tempo }`. The default is
48|`bhattacharyyaSimilarity`: both 8-emotion vectors renormalize to sum 1
49|(an all-zero vector gives an affinity of 0), `E` is the sum of
50|`sqrt(s_k * t_k)`, and the score is `0.70 * E` plus `0.15` each for
51|intensity and tempo closeness. `cosineSimilarity` over `buildFeatures`
52|output stays as an exported alternative. One exported object,
53|`MUSIC_CONFIG`, holds `similarity`, `weights`, `switchMargin` (0.07),
54|`dwellSec` (20), `minTrackSec` (45), `hardCutMargin` (0.20),
55|`crossfadeSec` (3), and `hardCutCrossfadeSec` (1.5). Everything else
56|reads from it. Ranking ties go to the lower track id.
57|
58|## Selection scheduler
59|
60|`core/music-schedule.ts` is a pure state machine. The reader calls
61|`observeScene`, `tickScheduler`, `requestNext`, and `noteTrackEnded`
62|with explicit `nowSec` values, so all timing is testable without
63|timers. State holds the current track id and when it started, the active
64|scene id, the pending scene id and since when, and the skip override
65|with the scene it belongs to.
66|
67|A newly entered scene becomes pending and the dwell clock restarts, so
68|fast scrolling keeps only the newest scene. The first track ever plays
69|at once with no dwell. After the pending scene holds for `dwellSec` it
70|becomes active and the override clears. Then the best track switches in
71|only when it beats the current score by `switchMargin` and the current
72|track played `minTrackSec`, unless it wins by `hardCutMargin` (hard
73|cut, short fade). A second passes the active scene back through the
74|switch check, so a hold from `minTrackSec` releases on time. A switch
75|reports its crossfade length: 3 s normally,
76|1.5 s for hard cuts. The skip choice holds until the next scene change;
77|after that, dwell and hysteresis apply with the override track as the
78|current track. A null scene means a failed analysis with no vector, so
79|it never triggers a switch. A non-looping track that ends fades into
80|the best remaining track, excluding the one that ended.
81|
82|## Change track
83|
84|`nextTrack` cycles tracks hand-labeled with the scene dominant emotion
85|(argmax of the renormalized scene vector, ties by emotion order), ranked
86|by score with ties by lower id, wrapping around and skipping the current
87|track. When the current track has another emotion, it starts at the top
88|candidate. With no other same-emotion track it falls back to the best
89|track overall that is not current. A null scene cycles all tracks in id
90|order. One track or none gives null, and the UI disables the button.
91|
92|## Player
93|
94|`app/player.tsx` takes the track, the fade length for the latest switch,
95|the scene title, a skip flag, and callbacks. It owns two `audio`
96|elements, play state, volume, and the equal-power crossfade
97|(cos/sin gains over the fade time, driven by `requestAnimationFrame`).
98|It never uses the `loop` attribute. Volume lives in a ref, so the slider
99|never re-runs the track effect or touches `src`. A new track request
100|mid-fade cancels the pending fade and fades from the audible element to
101|the newest track. On load each track seeks to `startSec` once metadata
102|is available. Long tracks with `loop` true crossfade into the other
103|element playing the same track from `startSec` when `currentTime`
104|reaches `duration - crossfadeSec`. When `loop` is false the player
105|reports the end and the scheduler picks the next-best track excluding
106|the ended one. Pause stops both elements; play resumes the audible one.
107|Audio starts only after the user presses play. Reduced motion is read in
108|state with a change listener and affects visuals only, never the fade.
109|
110|The bar shows Play/Pause, Volume, a Change track button (disabled when
111|Next has nothing to offer), the track title with its emotion label, and
112|attribution when present: composer or artist, license, and a source
113|link. On manifest failure the reader still renders and the bar shows a
114|short neutral note. UI motion stays under 200 ms. Controls are real
115|buttons and inputs with labels, visible focus, and keyboard use.
116|
117|## Image api
118|
119|Contract only, no routes. Request `{ bookId, textVersion, firstN, lastN
120|}` names the selection by touched paragraph ordinals. Response `{ url }`
121|is a Vercel Blob URL. The cache key is `firstN..lastN` plus
122|`textVersion` plus `promptVersion` at a deterministic Blob path with
123|`addRandomSuffix: false`. The server checks the path with `head()`
124|before generating and never returns bytes. The same paragraph range
125|reuses the image. Types live in `core/types.ts`.
126|
127|## Chat api
128|
129|Contract only, no routes. Request `{ bookId, textVersion, positionN,
130|spoilerMode, messages }` carries the chat history and the reader
131|position. The response is streamed text. The server builds context from
132|the book text up to `positionN`, or the whole book when `spoilerMode` is
133|on, with the book prefix first and the question last so readers share
134|the prompt cache. The system prompt answers only from that text and
135|refuses the rest. Types live in `core/types.ts`.
136|
137|## Quotas and budget
138|
139|Server only. Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars: reserve with
140|Redis `INCRBY` before each model call, refund with `DECRBY` after, one
141|reserve per call including retries. The server clamps every model tool
142|argument. Clients never see keys or raw errors. Generic messages go to
143|the client, details stay in server logs.
